correctness.rationale: For axis targets explicit one-parameter nonzero triples avoid finitely many t values. For nonzero coordinates use the multiplicative automorphism to normalize target (1,w), realize as an affine cubic Cw cut by e1=1,e2=w e3. Its projective completion has exactly six disallowed rational points (three infinity, three distinct zero-coordinate affine), and is nonsingular genus one except w=1 or w=9; these singular values have direct triple witnesses. Hasse q+1-2sqrt(q)>6 for q>=13 forces a valid rational point for every other nonzero w. Origin criterion e1=e2=0 becomes either characteristic 3 or split third roots of unity. Explicit exhaustive F11 check excludes (1,6). Independent exact prime-field enumeration q=11,13,17,19,23,29,31 agrees, but proof supplies all prime powers.

final_claim: For prime powers q>=13, 3Hq for Hq={(t,t^-1):t in Fq^x} equals all of Fq^2 if q divisible by 3 or q=1 mod3; otherwise it equals Fq^2 excluding origin. q=11 fails at target (1,6), proving the uniform threshold 13 sharp.
